text: If a man has a mind to be thought wiser, and a woman handsomer than they really are, their error is a comfortable one to themselves, and an innocent one with regard to other people; and I would rather make them my friends, by indulging them in it, than my enemies, by endeavoring (and that to no purpose) to undeceive them.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter XVII, to his son, London, October 16, Old Style 1747
